1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.strategy: Supports d4 and opens the diagonal of the king's bishop, so White can castle quickly behind a solid centre. The bishop on f4 stays outside the pawn chain instead of being shut in. Black must now decide how to challenge the centre.

Strikes at d4 at once, the freeing break Black wants in this structure. Black accepts that the pawn structure may change, with an isolated pawn or hanging pawns, in return for open lines for the bishops and active pieces.

Prepares to fianchetto the light-squared bishop, the piece usually shut in behind e6, onto the long diagonal, where it will eye the centre and support d5. Black plans to free the problem piece and keeps the central pawns intact.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack, Fianchetto Defence

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.strategy: Reinforces d5 with a pawn, so White's pressure on it counts for little. The light-squared bishop stays boxed in behind e6, so Black accepts a patient, slightly passive game in which freeing the position takes time.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack, Orthodox Defence

1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.strategy: Develops the second knight and covers e5, where the bishop on f4 points. The light-squared bishop stays shut in behind e6, so the set-up is solid but passive, and Black still has to find a way to free the position.
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Be7 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bf.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Harrwitz Attack, Two Knights Defence
